source_refs.note: Topic 10.2.1 with the Keep in Mind box, printed page 214.

blocks.text: The oxidation number of any atom or ion can be deduced from the oxidation number rules; an oxidation number refers to a single atom in a compound.

items: The oxidation number of any uncombined element is zero: each atom in S8, H2, Cl2, Na, Mg and Zn is zero.
In a compound or an ion, the more electronegative element is given the negative oxidation number: in HF, fluorine is -1.

Many atoms or ions have fixed oxidation numbers in compounds: group 1 alkali metals are always +1, group 2 alkaline earth elements always +2, group 17 halogens in binary compounds always -1, hydrogen is +1 (except in metal hydrides such as NaH, where it is -1), and oxygen is -2 (except in peroxides, where it is -1, and in F2O, where it is +2).
The oxidation number of an element in a monatomic ion equals the charge on the ion: Cl- is -1, Al3+ is +3.
The sum of the oxidation numbers in a compound is zero; in neutral molecules such as HCl and NaCl the algebraic sum for all the elements is zero.
In ions, the algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers equals the charge on the ion, as in CO3 2- and SO4 2-.

blocks.title: Keep in mind
blocks.text: Hydrogen is -1 with all metals and +1 with all non-metals. Oxygen is negative with all metals and with all non-metals except fluorine; oxygen is -2, -1 and -1/2 in H2O, Na2O2 and KO2 respectively. 'Ox. No.' is used as the abbreviation for oxidation number.

blocks.caption: Fixed values
rows: -1 in peroxides, +2 in F2O, -1/2 in KO2

blocks.prompt: Determine the oxidation number of oxygen in Na2O, iodine in ICl3, nitrogen in NO3- and chromium in K2Cr2O7 (Quick Check 10.1c).
blocks.explanation: Na2O: sodium +1 each, so O = -2. ICl3: chlorine is the more electronegative, -1 each, so I = +3. NO3-: N + 3(-2) = -1 gives N = +5. K2Cr2O7: 2(+1) + 2Cr + 7(-2) = 0 gives 2Cr = +12, Cr = +6.

items: Rules: element 0; more electronegative element negative; group 1 +1, group 2 +2, halogen -1 in binary compounds, H +1 (hydrides -1), O -2 (peroxides -1, F2O +2); monatomic ion = charge; sums are 0 for compounds and the charge for ions.
